name: Double Yukon (Solitaire)
description: Double Yukon is a massive, two-deck variation of the famous Yukon Solitaire. Unlike Klondike, all 104 cards are dealt into the tableau at once, with no stock or waste pile. The game is known for its 'group move' mechanic, allowing players to move any visible stack of cards regardless of their sequence, provided the base card of the stack fits the alternating-color building rule. This makes Double Yukon a deep, analytical game with high win rates for careful players.

content.text: Double Yukon is a massive, two-deck variation of the famous Yukon Solitaire. Unlike Klondike, all 104 cards are dealt into the tableau at once, with no stock or waste pile. The game is known for its 'group move' mechanic, allowing players to move any visible stack of cards regardless of their sequence, provided the base card of the stack fits the alternating-color building rule. This makes Double Yukon a deep, analytical game with high win rates for careful players.

Yukon Solitaire originated in the North American West during the late 19th-century gold rush era. The 'Double' variation appeared much later, popularized by digital solitaire suites that offered 104ndcard challenges to seasoned players.
One player only. Double Yukon is a solitaire (patience) game; the player plays alone against the layout, moving cards between tableau columns and to foundations with no opponent or partner.
Two card decks, large playing surface.

Cards are dealt into 10 columns. Column 1 has 5 cards (all face-up). Columns 2 through 10 have 7 to 15 cards respectively, with the last 6 cards in each column always face-up and the underlying cards face-down. There is no stock; all cards are on the table.
